title: Use dependency edges for ranked mixed-fidelity selection

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as deterministic review-profile graph distances from Git-changed paths with explicit projection reasons.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable critique 4: edges enable ranked repositories
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: With edges you can walk from task or touched files, include exact content within N hops, degrade to outline beyond, and omit the rest. That turns a repository into a ranked repository.
feedback.normalized_claim: Dependency edges should drive deterministic, budget-aware neighborhood selection and per-file fidelity rather than serving only as descriptive metadata.

current_behavior: The edge schema exists but generated packets declare module resolution unavailable.
Selection is explicit stdin, manifest, positional, or discovery input rather than a graph-ranked expansion from seed files or task entities.
Exact and numbered projections exist, but there is no outline-only file body projection or graph-distance policy.

proposal.summary: After edge extraction and projection tiers are credible, define a reproducible graph-ranking policy from declared task or file seeds to a bounded mixed-fidelity packet.
candidate_changes: Declare seed provenance, traversal direction, edge kinds, hop limits, scoring, tie-breaking, and budget stop rules.
Assign exact, outline, signature, or omitted posture by graph distance and role.
Emit a selection ledger explaining why each file received its rank and projection.
Evaluate review and bug-fixing accuracy against explicit-list and non-graph budget selection.
non_goals: Do not rank from incomplete or low-confidence edges without exposing that posture.
Do not infer a task from source content when no task or seed was supplied.
Do not let graph distance erase policy files, tests, or other non-import relevance.

questions: Which edge directions and kinds matter for review versus implementation tasks?
How are tests, configuration, docs, generated artifacts, and dynamically loaded modules ranked?
Can task text safely contribute seeds without granting source content instruction authority?
risks: Incomplete graphs can systematically omit critical context.
A single ranking policy may overfit TypeScript import graphs.
Selection provenance and scoring metadata can consume the savings it creates.
evidence_needed: Task-success benchmarks across ranking policies and token budgets.
Counterexamples involving dynamic dependencies, policies, and tests.
